lines: A bivalent is two homologous chromosomes paired
together. Each of them has two sister

Crossing over takes place between non-sister
chromatids — one chromatid of one homologue
with one chromatid of the other.
steps.why: Only chromatids belonging to DIFFERENT homologues carry different alleles of the same gene, so only an exchange between them can produce a new combination.
common_mistakes: Writing 'all four chromatids'. Only two of the four take part in one crossover.
Writing 'sister chromatids'. That is the opposite of the answer.
steps.memory_tip: Sisters are identical copies. Non-sisters come from the two different parents.
steps.margin_note: Say four chromatids first, then name the two that cross.

steps.label: Why not sisters

lines.text: Non-sister chromatids of the two homologous chromosomes — two of the four.

steps.why: The purpose of crossing over is new gene combinations, and moving material between two identical chromatids changes nothing. That is the reason the answer is non-sister and not sister.
common_mistakes: Answering with 'chiasmata' instead of naming the chromatids. A chiasma is the place, not the chromatid.
steps.memory_tip: Crossing over exchanges material between different chromosomes, never between two copies of the same one.
steps.margin_note: One sentence of reason is enough for the second mark.

insider_note: The word 'non-sister' is the mark. Adding 'of the homologous chromosomes' makes the answer complete.
